headline: Iran de-escalation lifts risk mood and trims the dollar's payroll gains before CPI
summary: The dollar index fell about 0.5% to near 101.75, giving back over half of Friday's jump, as Trump played down new strikes on Iran, oil slid and investors crowded into long-dollar trades took profit. The Aussie, pound and euro led, while the loonie and franc lagged, the Taiwan dollar slid on foreign outflows despite a stock rebound and the peso fell on weak growth.
drivers: Iran hopes and stretched positioning trim the dollar

Trump said new strikes on Iran were highly unlikely while talks go on, Brent fell nearly 6% to about $92.6 and stocks recovered from last week's AI rout. With speculators heavily long the dollar, the euro rose about 0.7% to near 1.1223 and the Aussie about 0.9% to near 0.6922.
Fed hike bets hold firm into CPI

December hike odds rose to about 85% from about 76% before Friday's payrolls, which limited the dollar's dip. Tuesday's October CPI is expected to show 0.3% headline and 0.2% core monthly gains, with annual inflation near 3.9%.
Oil and outflows split the laggards

The loonie was flat near 1.4117 as US crude fell about 3.5%. The Taiwan dollar slid to 32.882 even as the Taiex jumped 4.9%, because foreigners sold about NT$90bn of shares, while the won gained 9.5 to 1,347.1 on exporter dollar sales.
view: Still bullish for the next 1–2 weeks, but less stretched: the Fed is about 85% priced to hike in December while the RBA and BoC look done, and Monday's dip was a positioning wash-out rather than a change in rate spreads. I back the dollar against the loonie and Aussie, hold the euro short, and fade it only against the yen below Tokyo's 159–160 line. A DXY close below 101.50 or a core CPI print of 0.1% or less would turn me neutral.
ideas: Buy 1.4080–1.4100 as oil slides and Canada sheds jobs; for 1.4250, stop 1.4020.
Hold the short from 158.20–158.50 as the BoJ eyes December and Tokyo guards 160; for 156.50, stop 159.40.
Sell 0.6900–0.6920 with the RBA at its peak and the Fed still hiking; for 0.6780, stop 0.6970.
review: The USD/CAD buy filled at the 1.4077 low and is about 25 pips in favour, and the USD/JPY short is about 40 pips in favour near 157.93. The AUD/USD sale filled and is flat, the EUR/USD short is about 40 pips against me and the rupiah long about 30 points against, all inside their stops. I close the won buy at the 1,342 stop as exporters lifted the won, and keep every range call.

eurusd.note: Up about 0.7% to near 1.1223, recovering most of Friday's payrolls drop as risk appetite returned.
eurusd.why: The dollar did the moving. President Trump said fresh strikes on Iran were highly unlikely while talks continue, Brent fell nearly 6% to about $92.6 and investors rotated back into risk after last week's AI selloff. Positioning added fuel: speculators were heavily long the dollar, so even with December Fed hike odds up near 85%, the payroll gains were partly unwound.
eurusd.outlook: I keep the short from 1.1170–1.1190, now about 40 pips against me: rate spreads still favour the dollar and Tuesday's CPI can restore Friday's move. A close above 1.1260 would end the call.
eurusd.watch: US October CPI (Nov 10), Fed speakers, ECB speakers ahead of December, euro-zone sentiment data.

view.call: Short from 1.1170–1.1190; Fed hike odds near 85%.

gbpusd.note: Up about 0.75% to near 1.3441, back in the upper half of the 1.3280–1.3480 range.
gbpusd.why: The dollar did the moving as the Iran de-escalation story lifted risk assets and trimmed Friday's payroll-driven rally. Sterling also kept the support of high gilt yields after last week's BoE hike to 4%, with about 100bp of further tightening still priced. It rose about as much as the euro, so the move was a broad dollar story, not a UK one.
gbpusd.outlook: I keep the 1.3280–1.3480 range: BoE hike pricing supports dips, while a Fed set to hike in December caps rallies. A close above 1.3480 would open 1.3550.
gbpusd.watch: UK Q3 GDP and labour data, BoE speakers, US October CPI (Nov 10).

view.call: 1.3280–1.3480; hawkish BoE vs a hawkish Fed.

audusd.note: Up about 0.9% to near 0.6922, rebounding from Friday's seven-month low of 0.6855; the sale filled.
audusd.why: The dollar and risk mood did the moving. The Aussie is the market's favourite proxy for global risk, so it bounced as equities steadied, oil fell and US-Iran talks gathered pace. The rebound came from deeply oversold levels after a 2.5% weekly drop, and nothing domestic changed: swaps still give about an 80% chance that the RBA's 4.85% cash rate is the peak.
audusd.outlook: I keep the sale from 0.6900–0.6920 for 0.6780: the RBA looks done while the Fed is priced to hike, and the pair stays below its 200-day average near 0.7060. A close above 0.6970 would end the call.
audusd.watch: US October CPI (Nov 10), Australia jobs data, China activity data, AI-stock sentiment.

view.call: Sell 0.6900–0.6920; RBA has peaked, Fed still hiking.

usdjpy.note: Down about 0.35% to near 157.93; the short from 158.20–158.50 is about 40 pips in favour.
usdjpy.why: Both sides moved. The dollar slipped with lower oil and a better risk mood, while the yen drew support from the BoJ's September minutes, which showed broad agreement that further hikes are appropriate, and from ex-chief economist Kameda's view of a December move. Finance Ministry data also confirmed Tokyo spent a record ¥15.4tn over three days of intervention in the summer, a reminder of its resolve near 160.
usdjpy.outlook: I keep the short for 156.50: Tokyo's 159–160 line caps the upside and the BoJ leans toward a December hike. A close above 159.40 would end the call.
usdjpy.watch: US October CPI (Nov 10), Japan wage and GDP data, BoJ speakers, Tokyo comments near 159–160.

view.call: Short from 158.20–158.50; Tokyo's 160 line, BoJ hawkish.

usdchf.note: Little changed near 0.8194, one of only two G10 currencies not to gain on the dollar.
usdchf.why: The franc lost its haven bid. As investors moved back into risk assets on hopes of a US-Iran deal, the franc gave up the safety premium it had built during last week's selloff, offsetting the dollar's broad decline. SNB sight deposits fell to about CHF 452.9bn from 460.2bn, giving no sign of fresh intervention.
usdchf.outlook: I keep the 0.8130–0.8280 range: a hawkish Fed lifts the pair, but the franc regains demand on any new equity slide. A close above 0.8280 would open 0.8350.
usdchf.watch: US October CPI (Nov 10), Swiss inflation, SNB sight deposits, equity sentiment.

usdcad.note: Flat near 1.4117 after dipping to 1.4077; the buy filled and the loonie lagged every G10 peer but the franc.
usdcad.why: The loonie did the moving, against the dollar's broad slide. US crude fell about 3.5% to near $87.6 after Trump played down new strikes on Iran, hurting Canada's main export, and Friday's third straight monthly jobs loss keeps the BoC from matching a Fed that is about 85% priced to hike in December.
usdcad.outlook: I keep the buy from 1.4080–1.4100 for 1.4250: weak Canadian jobs and falling oil favour the dollar. A close below 1.4020 would end the call.
usdcad.watch: US October CPI (Nov 10), Canada inflation, BoC speakers, oil and US-Iran talks.

view.call: Buy 1.4080–1.4100; Canada jobs fall, oil slides.

usdcnh.note: Yuan slightly firmer near 6.673 offshore despite a 389-pip weaker-than-expected fixing at 6.7188.
usdcnh.why: Exporters did the moving. Seasonal year-end dollar sales offset the stronger dollar, even as the PBOC set the midpoint at 6.7188, its weakest since Oct 22 and well below the Reuters estimate, and banks raised dollar deposit rates to slow the rally. October data showed producer prices up 5.7%, the most in over four years, while consumer prices rose only 0.7%.
usdcnh.outlook: I keep the 6.64–6.70 range: Beijing is leaning against gains while exporters sell dollars on rallies. A close above 6.70 would show policymakers want a weaker yuan.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings vs estimates, China credit and activity data, FX reserve ratio rise (Nov 15).

view.call: 6.64–6.70; PBOC slows the yuan, exporters sell USD.

usdhkd.note: Little changed near 7.842, still close to the weak end of the 7.75–7.85 band.
usdhkd.why: Nothing local moved the pair. The gap between Hong Kong interbank rates and US rates still favours holding US dollars, and December Fed hike odds near 85% keep that gap wide. Chinese banks raising dollar deposit rates toward Hong Kong offshore levels adds a little competition for dollar funds.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in 7.83–7.85: the carry gap keeps it near 7.85, and only a jump in HIBOR or HKMA buying at 7.85 would pull it lower.
usdhkd.watch: HKMA operations at 7.85, HIBOR, US October CPI (Nov 10).

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Down about 0.3% to near 1.2786 in thin trade, with Singapore shut for Deepavali.
usdsgd.why: The dollar did the moving. With local markets closed for the holiday, the Singapore dollar simply tracked the broad dollar pullback as risk appetite improved and oil fell. It rose less than the euro or Aussie because the MAS policy band limits swings both ways.
usdsgd.outlook: I keep the 1.2740–1.2860 range: MAS's appreciating band supports the currency, but a Fed set to hike limits gains. A close above 1.2860 would open 1.2920.
usdsgd.watch: US October CPI (Nov 10), Singapore final Q3 GDP, Asian tech-stock flows.

usdkrw.note: Won rose 9.5 to 1,347.1 in Seoul and to about 1,340 in late trade; the buy was stopped at 1,342.
usdkrw.why: The won did the moving. Exporters sold dollars after last week's slide and AI-chip jitters eased, lifting the won to 1,346.7 intraday. Foreigners still sold about 693bn won of Kospi shares, a seventh straight session and about 13tn won in total, which kept the index down 0.8% and capped the gains until the weaker dollar in New York added more.
usdkrw.outlook: I close the long and move to a 1,330–1,365 range: exporter selling is now meeting persistent foreign outflows. A Seoul close above 1,365 would put the long back on.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign Kospi flows, Korean authorities' comments, AI-chip sentiment, US October CPI (Nov 10).

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar fell 11.4 cents to 32.882 in Taipei, hitting 32.957, even as the Taiex jumped 4.9%.
usdtwd.why: Foreign outflows did the moving. The stabilisation fund and new short-selling limits sent the Taiex up about 4.9%, but foreigners still sold about NT$90bn of shares and kept remitting proceeds from last week's NT$524bn of selling. Exporters sold dollars hard and the central bank steadied the market, so 33 held on turnover of about US$4.5bn across both venues, among the heaviest on record.
usdtwd.outlook: I keep the 32.60–33.05 range: officials are defending 33, but outflows keep pressing until foreigners turn buyers. A close above 33.05 would show the defence has failed.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows, TSMC October sales (Nov 10), stabilisation fund buying, central bank action.

usdmyr.note: No onshore trade: Malaysia was shut for the Deepavali holiday; Friday's close was 4.0565/0610.
usdmyr.why: Nothing local moved the ringgit because the Kuala Lumpur market was closed for the Deepavali replacement holiday. Offshore, the broad dollar pullback and lower oil were a mixed backdrop: risk appetite helps Asian currencies, but cheaper crude trims Malaysia's oil and gas income.
usdmyr.outlook: I keep the 4.035–4.085 range: Bank Negara's steady 2.75% rate supports the ringgit, but a Fed set to hike limits gains.
usdmyr.watch: Malaysia Q3 GDP and trade data, regional chip stocks, US October CPI (Nov 10).

usdphp.note: Peso fell 25.5 centavos to 63.31 at the BAP close, a third straight loss, on weak Q3 growth.
usdphp.why: The peso did the moving. Third-quarter growth slowed to 2.1%, the weakest since early 2021 and well below forecasts, which raises doubts about a December BSP hike. The dollar's strength in Asian hours after Friday's payrolls added to the pressure; the dollar's later fall in New York came after Manila had closed.
usdphp.outlook: I keep the 62.70–63.50 range but favour the top half: weak growth hurts the peso, while remittance season and cheaper oil limit losses. A close above 63.50 would put 64 back in view.
usdphp.watch: BSP comments after the GDP miss, oil, US October CPI (Nov 10), BSP decision (Dec 17).

usdidr.note: Rupiah edged 4 points firmer to 18,085, after trading between about 18,070 and 18,110.
usdidr.why: The rupiah did little. Stable reserves of about $146.8bn and a rise in consumer confidence to 119.9 helped it recover from early losses, while the strong dollar in Asian hours capped gains. Bank Indonesia's JISDOR reference rate improved to 18,103 from 18,130.
usdidr.outlook: I keep the long from 18,100–18,130, now about 30 points against me, for 18,300: a Fed set to hike and MSCI-related outflow risk outweigh steady data. A close below 18,060 would end the call.
usdidr.watch: US October CPI (Nov 10), Bank Indonesia operations, MSCI index review, foreign bond flows.

view.call: Long from 18,100–18,130; Fed hikes, outflow risk.

usdinr.note: Rupee ended a five-day winning streak near 93.93 after touching a six-month high of 93.69.
usdinr.why: The RBI did the moving. Cheaper crude, foreign equity inflows and a softer dollar lifted the rupee to 93.69 early, but state-run banks bought dollars at the central bank's behest ahead of a local holiday, pushing it back to about where it closed Friday. Analysts put support at 93.50 and resistance at 94.30.
usdinr.outlook: I keep the 93.50–94.50 range: oil and inflows favour the rupee, but RBI dollar buying caps gains. A Brent close back above $105 would push it toward 94.50.
usdinr.watch: US October CPI (Nov 10), oil and US-Iran talks, RBI dollar buying, India inflation data.

view.call: 93.50–94.50; oil and inflows vs RBI buying.

eurjpy.note: Up about 0.4% to near 177.2 as the euro rose more than the yen; mid-range.
eurjpy.why: The euro did the moving. It gained about 0.7% on the dollar as risk appetite returned, while the yen rose only about 0.35% on hawkish BoJ minutes. That left the cross higher, back toward the middle of its range.
eurjpy.outlook: I keep the 175.5–178.0 range: a hawkish BoJ caps rallies, while Japan's fiscal worries limit dips. A close above 178.0 would open 179.
eurjpy.watch: Tokyo comments, Japan wage and GDP data, ECB speakers, equity sentiment.

view.call: 175.5–178.0; risk mood vs a hawkish BoJ.

cnhjpy.note: Down about 0.3% to near 23.67 as the yen firmed and the yuan held steady.
cnhjpy.why: The yen did the moving. It gained on the dollar after the BoJ minutes kept December hike bets alive, while the yuan barely moved as exporters' dollar sales offset a much weaker PBOC fixing. That pulled the cross back into the middle of its range.
cnhjpy.outlook: I keep the 23.3–23.9 range: Beijing is slowing the yuan and the BoJ leans hawkish, so neither leg should run far.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, China activity data, FX reserve ratio rise (Nov 15), Tokyo comments.

watch: Next: US October CPI (Nov 10) and PPI (Nov 13), Fed speakers, US-Iran talks and oil, TSMC October sales (Nov 10), the PBOC's FX reserve hike (Nov 15) and the Fed and BoJ in December, plus Tokyo's 159–160 line, Taiwan's defence of 33 and foreign flows out of Asian chip stocks.
